claim: CMO is an out-of-fold two-party margin-overperformance measure rather than wins added.
publication_note: Retain explicit noncausal language.

claim: Larry Means moved from approximately -6 CMO in 2010 to +29 in 2014.
publication_note: Round to whole points.

claim: Letson's legislative margin stayed near -1 in 2010 and -5 in 2014 while the statewide baseline fell from roughly -15 to -33.
publication_note: Present as descriptive realignment, not causal effect.

claim: Ledbetter posted about +22 CMO as a Democrat in 2010 and won the same district as a Republican in 2014.
publication_note: Party-switch ideology evidence is retrospective.

claim: Beddingfield posted about +23 CMO and was out-raised by more than two-to-one.
publication_note: Finance story reports about $60k versus $145k.

claim: Barbara Boyd was near the progressive side of her caucus and posted about +40 CMO in 2010.
publication_note: Describe percentile rather than ideological label alone.

claim: Figures was around the 23rd conservative percentile and sponsored 2010 firearm safe-storage legislation.
publication_note: Bill summary establishes direction; do not imply enactment.

claim: Daniels's production CMO is about +56 and geography-refit range is about +48 to +56.
publication_note: Always display the range with the headline value.

claim: Drummond's production CMO is about +30 and geography-refit range is about +13 to +30.
publication_note: Always display the range with the headline value.

claim: Among 52 clean through-2018 matches Spearman CMO versus Shor score is about -0.03 with clustered interval roughly [-0.32,+0.25].
publication_note: Descriptive selected sample; not causal.

claim: Cycle correlations are about -0.48 in 2010 and +0.55 in 2014.
publication_note: Only three clean 2018 matches.

claim: Among five scored pairs the higher-CMO candidate is more conservative once, more progressive twice, and broadly similar twice.
publication_note: State pair-selection limitations.

claim: Simple legislative service years have near-zero rank relationship with CMO.
publication_note: Add a generated tenure exhibit before publication.

claim: Betterton's economically progressive issue page was published and last modified before the 2014 general election.
publication_note: WordPress publication metadata makes the code temporally eligible; retain local tenure as a competing explanation.

claim: 2014 geographic allocation materially changes several headline CMO estimates.
publication_note: Use interval glyphs rather than exact rank ordering.

claim: Linda Meigs recorded about +15.1 Total OOF CMO and +9.7 resource-adjusted CMO while supporting Medicaid expansion and an education lottery.
publication_note: Keep the platform and resource-adjustment claims distinct.

claim: Kim Caudle Lewis recorded about +15.0 Total OOF CMO and +15.8 resource-adjusted CMO while combining education and reproductive-rights positioning with business and chamber credentials.
publication_note: Describe chamber and business service as competing valence evidence.

claim: James Fields recorded about +15.6 CMO and a 34-point raw gap over the statewide baseline; his roll-call score was mildly conservative while he supported new school revenue.
publication_note: Lead with mixed ideology and cross-racial local membership.

claim: Rex Cheatham recorded about +16.7 CMO that survives resource adjustment; pre-election evidence establishes strong education-labor alignment but not cultural positions.
publication_note: Leave guns and abortion unknown.

claim: Napoleon Bracy's +20.7 CMO falls to about +12.9 after fundraising adjustment; his later roll-call score is temporally ineligible for 2010.
publication_note: Do not backcast post-election ideology.

claim: Greg Varner's +15.5 CMO falls to about +8.4 after fundraising adjustment and his opponent Gerald Dial brought prior Democratic tenure.
publication_note: Treat as finance and opponent-identity evidence.

claim: Jerry Fielding recorded about +18.2 CMO after a 26-year judicial career and faced a Republican replacement selected roughly eight weeks before Election Day; later cultural positions are not valid 2010 codes.
publication_note: Separate demonstrated local/opponent mechanisms from later ideology.

claim: David Beddingfield recorded about +23 CMO despite a two-to-one fundraising disadvantage and entered the race with years as Fort Payne school-board president.
publication_note: Treat local education credibility as demonstrated; full ideology remains unknown.

claim: Dennis Stephens signed an anti-corruption pledge but faced a Republican nominee with demonstrated primary strength; his substantive ideology remains unknown.
publication_note: Do not infer issue positions from the unrecovered interview.

claim: Jeff McLaughlin recorded about +37.7 CMO despite an approximately eight-to-one fundraising disadvantage; his pre-election roll-call score was on the conservative side of his Democratic caucus while his campaign stressed education, infrastructure, TVA, and clean government.
publication_note: Describe the ideological bundle and prior-service mechanism rather than reducing it to one dimension.

claim: Richard Lindsey and John Robinson occupied the same broad conservative Democratic ideology band and both had AEA support, yet their 2014 CMO differed by about 36 points; resource adjustment explains only about five points of the gap.
publication_note: Use as the principal within-era evidence against an ideology-only explanation.

claim: The production Drummond-Alexander CMO gap is about 22.5 points, but geography sensitivity narrows its lower bound below one point; both ideology scores are post-election and opponent resources strongly differ.
publication_note: Do not treat this pair as causal evidence that progressive ideology increased CMO.

claim: Henry White exceeded Jennifer Marsden by about 53 CMO points, but White's own CMO changed by roughly 34 points against the same opponent; Marsden faced a twenty-year incumbent who shared conditional support for Medicaid expansion and she approximately matched the prior Democrat's vote share.
publication_note: Use the pair as evidence that ideology, opponent incumbency, and local roots cannot be separated by the matched score alone.

claim: Johnny Mack Morrow recorded about +28 CMO in the 2014 House race and +31 in the 2018 Senate race; direct 2014 evidence establishes armed-school-security policy, public-school investment, and constituency service, while the explicit pro-life and pro-Second Amendment campaign framing is documented in 2018.
publication_note: Keep the election-specific chronology explicit and do not backdate the 2018 abortion language.

claim: Larry Means exceeded Darrell Turner by about 25 CMO points, but resource adjustment reduces the gap to about 13; both emphasized working families and public education, while Turner's cultural positions remain unobserved.
publication_note: Present as compatible with cultural differentiation, not as an estimate of its effect.

claim: Independent identity-redacted review produced exact agreement on 40 of 46 candidate-dimension codes; all six disagreements concerned intensity rather than direction, and all six were explicitly adjudicated.
publication_note: Report raw agreement and the adjudication process; do not describe the codes as unanimously validated.
